I read the whole supplied source, lines 1–81. It has one theorem, `solution`. It declares no definitions, simp lemmas, simp attributes, `@[simp]` or `@[simps]` annotations, or simp sets. So there is no simp interface to evaluate: no orientation choice, no competing rules, and nothing that could cause unwanted expansion or a rewrite cycle.

The proof calls `simp`, `simp only` and `split_ifs <;> simp` as ordinary tactics. In `hΨ_tmul` the `simp only [...]` is followed by `rfl`. That is local proof style, not a gap in a simp interface. I did not look into whether Mathlib lacks a simp lemma for `piScalarRight` applied to a tensor product. Doing so would not tie to any declaration in this file, and the rubric warns against recommending simp attributes just because an identity looks simple. I found no concrete, source-supported simp-interface defect in this file. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim about simplifier behaviour.
